accuracy.evidence: Checked against USGS (Earthquake Hazards Program FAQ: about 81% of the world's largest earthquakes occur along the circum-Pacific belt; This Dynamic Earth on plate boundaries), NOAA Ocean Exploration (Ring of Fire about 40,000 km long with about 450 volcanoes, about 75% of active volcanoes) and National Geographic's Ring of Fire reference. The ring path runs New Zealand, Tonga, Vanuatu, Papua New Guinea, the Molucca Sea, Philippines, Taiwan, Japan, Kurils, Kamchatka, Aleutians, Alaska, Cascadia, California, Mexico, Central America and the Andes to southern Chile, with the Sunda arc through Java and Sumatra as a branch. Plate pairs named for tapped quakes match the USGS plate map (for example Nazca and South American off Chile, Cocos and Caribbean in Central America). The Alpide belt and rare intraplate quakes are kept on the map so the pattern is not overstated, and the adult text says the map is a simple picture, not to scale. Plate speed (a few cm a year, like fingernails) follows USGS.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented misconceptions (Dove 1998 and King 2008 on pupils' ideas about earthquakes and volcanoes; Earth Science Literacy Principles): quakes and volcanoes being random or evenly spread (step 1 prediction, challenge 'rand', m8), caused by heat or a hot climate (challenge 'hot', m7), caused by cities or people (step 4 prediction, challenge 'city'), the name taken literally as real fire (challenge 'fire', m1), and the middle of a big country being as likely to have a big quake (challenge 'mid', step 5 pins, m6). Volcanoes being somewhere else is the step 2 prediction.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrfire is about the global pattern: a Pacific-centred world map where batches of seeded earthquake dots fall along plate-edge lines, volcano triangles land on the same lines, a finger trace lights 12 stops from New Zealand to Chile, tapping a quake names the two plates that meet there under dashed plate edges, and eight place pins test on or off the ring. flagearthq explains what happens in one earthquake and flagvolc the inside of one volcano; neither maps where they happen. lab_distinct gate passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The pattern is discovered, not told: after the first batch the dots already form lines and the live count says how many sit round the Pacific edge; volcanoes then land on the same lines; tracing the dots draws the horseshoe; plate edges appear only in step 4 and every tapped ring quake names a plate pair, while a stray inland quake is called rare and far from an edge; the pins step checks the idea against new places.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'spread out evenly all over the world' (90 dots fall in lines), 'volcanoes are somewhere else' (triangles land on the quake lines) and 'big cities make the ground weak' (dots sit along plate edges in empty ocean trenches and Alaska, not by city size).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; wrong options carry five distinct messages: random or even spread, the middle of a plate, heat or climate as the cause, people or cities as the cause, and the name read as real fire. Answer order rotates.

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and concrete comparisons (a giant horseshoe, plates moving as fast as fingernails grow) and names the ring's path by real places. Canvas labels are a few words. The young layout gives 56 px buttons. The adult text names NGSS 4-ESS2-2 and the KS2 geography wording with key vocabulary. validate_lessons readability passes.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Kid paragraphs cover the pattern, the ring's path, why plates cause it, and what the name does and does not mean. Items mix locating the pattern (p1, m2, m8), proportion on the ring (p2, m4), cause (p3, m5, m7), counting volcanoes (p4), on or off the ring (p5, m6), the name (m1), plate speed in numbers (m3) and in words (m9).

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 light and 360 px Android dark screenshots of every step at the start and after Show me. The map fills the stage width with 3 px dots and 5 px triangles on phones so lines read clearly; trace stops are 7 px circles with a 22 px hit radius; pins have a 26 px hit radius and white name tags; header and footer chips shrink to fit. The ocean and land colours switch for dark theme, and the dashed plate edges turn yellow on dark.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: Add 30 earthquakes, Add 20 volcanoes, Trace the next part, Check a quake, and one button per place pin. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with how many quakes sit round the Pacific edge, the volcano count, the ring stops lit, the plate pair for each checked quake and whether a place is on the ring and why. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
